memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "For Aaron and his sons, they made tunics of fine linen - the work of a weaver - and the turban of fine linen, the linen caps and the undergarments of finely twisted linen. The sash was made of finely twisted linen and blue, purple and scarlet yarn - the work of an embroiderer - as the Lord commanded Moses." - Exod 39:27-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Tunics, turban, caps, undergarments, sash. God specified the priest's clothing right down to what nobody would ever see.

The undergarments are worth noticing. They were mentioned for the sake of modesty and reverence (Exod 28:42-43). God cared about what was under the robe as much as what was on it.

We are so easily satisfied with the visible layer. As long as the outer garment looks right, we assume all is well. God's concern goes deeper — He looks at the heart (1 Sam 16:7), and He examines the parts of us that never appear in public.

Notice too that this clothing was for "Aaron and his sons," not Aaron alone. A whole family of priests, all clothed, all serving.

That anticipates something wonderful. Peter tells ordinary believers that they are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation (1 Pet 2:9). We are not spectators watching a priest in special robes. In Christ, every believer has been brought into priestly service.

And every one of us is clothed by God's provision, not our own tailoring. He has clothed me with garments of salvation (Isa 61:10).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are the hidden parts of your life as well kept as the visible ones?
2. Do you see yourself as part of a royal priesthood?
3. What are you still trying to tailor for yourself that God has already provided?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, clothe me completely — not just where people can see. Thank You for making me Yours and giving me a place to serve. Amen.
